title: Starbucks Thanksgiving hours
summary: Many locations are expected to open for the holiday, but customers may encounter shorter hours.
content: Thanksgiving morning generally starts with a familiar routine at my house: coffee. If there is an airport pick-up on the schedule, or a last-minute grocery store run, it might even include driving through a Starbucks. But I’ve learned to check my Starbucks app to see which locations are open before I head out. Thanksgiving falls on Thursday, Nov. 26, and while many Starbucks locations will be open on the holiday, some will operate on reduced hours, according to the company’s website . Individual locations can have different schedules, and some may even be closed. The holiday arrives as Starbucks shows signs of progress in its turnaround effort. The company reported stronger comparable sales and improved operating margins for fiscal 2026, although it also closed hundreds of North American locations as it reassessed its store portfolio. Also read: How much SBUX stock does Starbucks CEO Brian Niccol actually own? Is Starbucks open on Thanksgiving 2026? Starbucks does not operate on a nationwide Thanksgiving schedule. Customers can check the Starbucks app or store locator for location-specific hours. Store hours can also vary based on location type. Coffeehouses in airports, hospitals, and hotels may operate on different schedules. Licensed locations inside grocery stores, malls, and other businesses may follow the host property’s holiday hours. Related: Kroger is open on Thanksgiving, but there’s a catch Calling the store directly is another way to confirm its schedule. While many Starbucks locations will be open on Thanksgiving, some will operate on reduced hours, and others will close. CFOTO / Getty Images Starbucks’ turnaround is showing results The holiday season is an important period for Starbucks, which has been working to reverse a prolonged sales slowdown and improve the customer experience under CEO Brian Niccol. The company’s fiscal 2026 results, reported Oct. 29, showed improvement in several key measures: 6.2%: Increase in global comparable coffeehouse sales 6.5%: Increase in U.S. comparable coffeehouse sales 3.4%: Increase in U.S. comparable transactions $37.9 billion: Full-year consolidated revenue, up 2% from fiscal 2025 9.7%: Full-year GAAP operating margin, up 180 basis points year over year $2.21: Full-year GAAP earnings per share, up 36% from the prior year Source: Starbucks Q4 and full fiscal year 2026 report The fourth quarter also showed momentum. Global comparable coffeehouse sales increased 7.2%, while U.S. comparable sales rose 7.7%. U.S. transactions increased by 2.4%, suggesting that more customers were visiting stores rather than that sales growth was driven entirely by higher average spending. CEO Brian Niccol described the shift in the company’s Oct. 29, 2026 earnings release : “Back to Starbucks started as our turnaround plan. Now, it’s our growth plan.” The results are encouraging, but they do not mean the turnaround is complete. Starbucks is still working to balance customer experience, labor investments, store operations, and profitability. Store closures show the company is still making changes Starbucks also made significant changes to its North American store base during fiscal 2026. In September, the company closed approximately 250 company-operated coffeehouses in North America, as reported on TheStreet . Starbucks said the locations did not deliver the coffeehouse experience or financial performance it expected from the brand. More Restaurants: 40-year-old fast-food franchisee files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy Landry’s rescues 9 restaurants from bankruptcy as closures mount Outback Steakhouse restaurant franchisee files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy The closures were part of its effort to strengthen the store portfolio under the Back to Starbucks strategy. At the end of fiscal 2026 , Starbucks operated 41,607 coffeehouses worldwide, including 16,781 in the United States. The company has said it sees continued opportunity for growth in North America. But the closures underscore the challenge of improving performance while maintaining a large retail footprint. Restaurant prices remain part of the consumer equation Starbucks is also operating in an environment where consumers continue to face higher food and restaurant prices. The U.S. Department of Agriculture’s October 2026 food-price update reported that prices for food away from home, which includes restaurant and foodservice purchases, were 4% higher than a year earlier. Grocery food prices increased 2.2% over the same period. Those figures provide context for consumer spending, but they do not specifically measure increases in Starbucks menu prices. As for Thanksgiving, anyone preparing a feast for family and friends might welcome having someone else make coffee to get the day started, so a stop at Starbucks might be just what the chef needs. title: Best Buy, Target, Kohl’s bring back classic Black Friday tradition
summary: Retailers have spent years changing Black Friday. Now some are betting shoppers still want the experience they left behind.
content: Kohl’s, Best Buy, and Target want to bring back the classic Black Friday where customers line up early in exchange for the best deals and special giveaways. Now that most retailers have opted to stay closed on Thanksgiving, you would think that Black Friday would become an even bigger shopping day. That, however, hasn’t happened, and the tradition of waking up early in order to get the best promotions, deals, and “doorbusters” from your favorite stores has lessened. It’s a subtle shift, not a major one. “Black Friday 2025 didn’t kill the holiday; it changed how shoppers approached it,” said Joe Shasteen, Global Head of Advanced Analytics at RetailNext. More Target: Best Buy offers a price match policy Target dropped Target makes a big mistake with its latest pricing decision Target has a problem that sends shoppers to Amazon Shoppers, he noted, were behaving more thoughtfully. “Foot traffic was down 3.6% on Friday and 8.6% on Saturday, but that wasn’t disinterest. It was intention. Shoppers showed they’re done with the impulse-driven, one-day frenzy. Prices, tariffs, and tighter budgets pushed people to shop with discipline, not adrenaline, and they responded by turning Black Friday into a value calculation.” For 2026, Kohl’s, Target, and Best Buy are joining JCPenney, which never stopped trying to make Black Friday an early morning event by going back to offering special deals, promotions, and giveaways for the first customers through their doors on the Friday after Thanksgiving. TheStreet Target, Best Buy, Kohl’s, and JCPenney want early Black Friday shoppers Retailers enter the holiday season facing a consumer base that plans to shop, but will broadly be more careful with its dollars. “Consumers have made it clear they are willing to make sacrifices for the things that matter to them this holiday season, but they are making careful decisions about when and where they spend to make that money go further,” ICSC CEO Tom McGee said in his company’s 2026 Holiday Intent Survey . Retailers, he added, are going to have to do more to bring customers in. “Shoppers remain resilient, but they’re more discerning and value-conscious; competitive prices, convenient shopping options, and experiences that bring people together are non-negotiable for retailers to attract shoppers and give them reasons to return throughout the season,” he added. Target, Kohl’s, Best Buy, and JCPenney all have offers designed to get customers lined up before opening on Black Friday: Target: The first 100 eligible shoppers at every store on Black Friday, Nov. 27, get a gift card worth $25, $50, or $100, and one per store gets $1,000. Last year it was tote bags, according to a press release . Kohl’s: The first 200 shoppers at every store on Nov. 27 get $5 to $100 in instant Kohl’s Cash. Stores open at 5 a.m., Kohl’s shared in a press release . Best Buy: My Best Buy members can buy a $100 gift card for $60 on Nov. 27, in stores only, Chain Store Age reported. JCPenney: The 5 a.m., 9 a.m., 1 p.m., and 5 p.m. giveaways are a yearly tradition, and they will return, according to the company’s website . Kohl’s will also give the first 200 shoppers at each store on Saturday, Nov. 28 , a Sephora at Kohl’s promotional coupon worth $5 to $100 for beauty purchases that day. RTM Nexus CEO Dominick Miserandino thinks these retailers are smart to try to capture dollars early. “I think it’s a good move. Once you get them in the store, it’s a much easier conversion event. Plus, it speaks straight to people’s wallets,” he told TheStreet. As a former general manager of a large toy store, I see the value of trying to capture early dollars, but question going back to the madness of trying to get customers to line up in the early morning. In the past, that led to fights, injuries, and hurt feelings. There are better ways to spread out the promotions, or randomize them more in order to still attract people, but not create a dangerous situation. Target is trying to get customers to its stores early on Black Friday. Shutterstock Thanksgiving weekend shopping remains strong A record 202.9 million consumers shopped during the five-day holiday weekend from Thanksgiving Day through Cyber Monday, according to the 2025 annual consumer survey from the National Retail Federation and Prosper Insights & Analytics. That figure is up from 197 million shoppers last year and surpasses the previous record of 200.4 million set in 2023. The total also exceeds NRF’s initial expectations of 186.9 million shoppers over the holiday weekend. The survey showed that stores remain important. A total of 129.5 million consumers shopped in-store , up 3% from 126 million in 2024. Online saw 134.9 million shoppers , up 9% from 124.3 million last year. Black Friday remains the top shopping day for both in-store and online, attracting 80.3 million in-store shoppers and 85.7 million online, slightly below last year’s totals of 81.7 million and 87.3 million, respectively. Saturday drew 62.7 million in-store consumers , up slightly from 61.1 million in 2024, and 63 million online compared with 53.9 million last year. The Sunday after Thanksgiving drew a record 32.6 million in-store shoppers, a 27% increase over the 25.6 million who shopped in 2024. And 38.7 million shopped online on Sunday, compared with 32.8 million last year. “Thanksgiving weekend is an important time for families and friends to come together, and holiday shopping plays a key role in that shared experience,” said NRF CEO Matthew Shay. For 2026, an estimated 182.7 million consumers plan to shop during Thanksgiving weekend, down slightly from 186.9 million last year. Black Friday remains the most popular day, with 126 million holiday shoppers planning to shop. The survey also found that 59% of holiday shoppers plan to use AI to support their holiday shopping. title: BJ’s joins Costco, Sam’s Club in Thanksgiving Day store closings
summary: The warehouse retailer confirmed its holiday schedule to TheStreet, including extended shopping hours for Black Friday and the days before Christmas.
content: Forgetting an ingredient for Thanksgiving dinner could prove more costly than usual this year, especially for shoppers accustomed to saving money by buying in bulk. Several of the nation’s largest retailers are closing their doors for the holiday, leaving shoppers with fewer options for last-minute grocery runs. While Thanksgiving Day was once considered the unofficial start of Black Friday shopping, many major retailers have returned to closing their stores on the holiday, even as their Black Friday sales have begun earlier. Also Read: Target closes stores on Thanksgiving, but has a Black Friday surprise That includes Walmart , its membership warehouse chain Sam’s Club, and Costco , as TheStreet previously reported. Parade and the Associated Press also report widespread holiday closures. BJ’s Wholesale Club (BJ) is following a similar holiday strategy, balancing Thanksgiving and Christmas closures with extended shopping hours on some of the busiest days of the season. The timing of this year’s holiday also means shoppers have just four weeks between Thanksgiving and Christmas to finish their holiday shopping. For shoppers who need groceries on Thursday, the closure means looking beyond the major warehouse clubs. Whole Foods Market and some other grocery chains will have locations open on Thanksgiving, though many will operate with reduced hours. Checking local store hours before leaving home could save an unnecessary trip. Retailers are offering Black Friday deals ahead of the holiday, but shoppers who prefer to visit a warehouse club in person will need to plan around the closure. title: Target, Kohl’s and JCPenney use Black Friday freebies to lure shoppers
summary: Shoppers can score free gift cards worth up to $1,000, collectible snow globes and other surprises — if they get there early.
content: Black Friday shoppers won’t necessarily need to open their wallets to walk away with something valuable this year. From gift cards worth as much as $1,000 at Target to collectible snow globes and diamond earrings at JCPenney , major retailers are offering shoppers extra incentives to visit stores Friday, Nov. 27. And at Kohl’s , shoppers will have a second reason to set their alarms early Saturday morning. The giveaways come as retailers face growing competition for shoppers’ attention, both online and in stores, with artificial intelligence adding another layer to the battle for holiday spending. Also Read: When Walmart, Target, Costco, and other major retailers open on Black Friday “Historically, Black Friday was about being the first to a deal. Now shoppers are increasingly asking AI to hunt down these deals for them,” Anjee Solanki, national director of retail services and practice groups at Colliers U.S., told TheStreet. About one in three likely Black Friday and Cyber Monday shoppers plan to use AI this year, more than double last year, Solanki said. But some of the holiday weekend’s most valuable promotions will require shoppers to leave their couches. “Retailers need to offer an attractive incentive for shoppers to visit their store first,” retail analyst Bruce Winder told TheStreet. Winder expects slightly longer lines this Black Friday as consumers facing affordability pressures go to greater lengths to save money. Why retailers are betting on Black Friday freebies With holiday discounts starting weeks before Thanksgiving, retailers have to work harder to draw crowds on Black Friday itself. “Black Friday is still a huge day, but it’s not as special as it used to be,” Neil Saunders, managing director of retail at GlobalData, told TheStreet. Winder said incentives that translate into immediate savings can be particularly effective as consumers grapple with affordability challenges. But giveaways alone won’t necessarily keep shoppers coming back. “Gimmicks can work, but people want their shopping experiences to be worthwhile,” Saunders said. More Retail: Black Friday 2026: These retailers offer the biggest discounts Black Friday shoppers face a surprising AI pricing twist JCPenney’s Black Friday sale starts early, but an old tradition remains Where to find Black Friday 2026 giveaways For shoppers hoping to score multiple freebies, planning ahead could pay off. Some giveaways begin before stores officially open, while others are staggered throughout the day. Here’s what five major retailers are giving away this holiday weekend. Target, Kohl’s, JCPenney, Lowe’s and Michaels are offering Black Friday freebies and giveaways to entice shoppers to visit stores in 2026. Target stores open at 6 a.m. local time Friday following the retailer’s nationwide Thanksgiving closure. Giveaway tickets are expected to be distributed beginning around 5 a.m. and must be redeemed during the first hour of business. However, the gift cards can be saved for future purchases. No purchase is necessary, and shoppers must be at least 13 years old. Additional details are available on Target’s Black Friday giveaway page . Kohl’s offers two days of Black Friday freebies Kohl’s is giving shoppers two opportunities to score freebies, including its first Sephora at Kohl’s giveaway. Friday, Nov. 27: The first 200 shoppers at each store will receive a surprise envelope containing $5 to $100 in promotional Kohl’s Cash. Saturday, Nov. 28: The first 200 shoppers at each store will receive a Sephora at Kohl’s promotional gift coupon worth $5 to $100. Kohl’s stores open at 5 a.m. Black Friday. The retailer is also running a sweepstakes from Nov. 27 through Nov. 30 with prizes including gift cards, product bundles and a $10,000 cash grand prize. JCPenney Black Friday snow globes, coupons return For some JCPenney shoppers, Black Friday isn’t just about finding deals. It’s also about adding another collectible snow globe to their holiday collections. Having covered and shopped JCPenney’s Black Friday sales for years, I’ve seen firsthand how the retailer’s giveaways have become a holiday tradition. “Last year, some shoppers began lining up before 2 a.m., highlighting that Black Friday remains as much an event as it is a shopping occasion,” JCPenney CEO Michelle Wlazlo told TheStreet. While JCPenney’s Black Friday sale started a week early, the retailer is saving some of its biggest surprises for the holiday weekend. Stores open at 5 a.m. local time Black Friday, with giveaways scheduled throughout the day: 5 a.m.: Mystery savings coupons and limited-edition Harry Potter-themed Hogwarts Express snow globes, while supplies last. 9 a.m.: A chance to win a Ninja dual-basket air fryer ($270 value). 1 p.m.: A chance to win lab-grown diamond stud earrings ($600 value). 5 p.m.: A chance to win Samsonite hardside luggage ($220 value). Additional giveaways are scheduled for Saturday and Sunday. Shoppers can find the full schedule and eligibility requirements on JCPenney’s Black Friday giveaways page . “Black Friday remains one of the few retail moments that brings entire families together in person, and we continue to see that reflected in our stores,” Wlazlo said. Lowe’s brings back Black Friday mystery buckets Lowe’s is bringing back its mystery bucket giveaway, giving early Black Friday shoppers a chance to take home free merchandise. The promotion is available to eligible MyLowe’s Rewards and MyLowe’s Pro Rewards members, while supplies last. Both loyalty programs are free to join. Stores open at 6 a.m. local time Black Friday. Additional details are available on Lowe’s Black Friday events page . Michaels offers free Black Friday countdown calendars Michaels is giving away approximately 500 free holiday countdown calendars per participating store beginning Black Friday as part of its Countdown to Craftsmas promotion , the company said. The 25-day Advent calendars feature craft projects, decorating tips, exclusive offers and in-store events. One calendar per participating store is expected to contain a $100 gift card, and one shopper nationwide will win a $10,000 cash prize. No purchase is necessary. Eligible shoppers ages 18 and older can request a free calendar from a store associate and open the Black Friday door to see if they’ve won. Michaels stores open at 7 a.m. local time Black Friday. The official giveaway rules put the odds of finding a $100 gift card at approximately 1 in 500. title: Bank with 227-year history closes dozens of branches nationwide
summary: Although Chase plans more shutdowns, its overall footprint is another story.
content: One of the oldest financial institutions in the U.S. is closing dozens of retail branches nationwide as the shift toward digital banking continues to reshape the industry. With more consumers turning to mobile apps and online platforms to manage their finances, traditional banks are reassessing their physical footprints. While some lenders are scaling back their brick-and-mortar networks, others are investing in new locations to maintain access to in-person services. Chase is taking both approaches, closing dozens of branches while continuing to expand and renovate locations across the country. JPMorgan Chase traces its roots to 1799, when The Manhattan Company was founded in New York City. Today, it operates one of the largest banking networks in the U.S. through its Chase consumer and commercial banking business. Chase closes dozens of retail branches nationwide Chase closed 23 branches between Aug. 21 and Oct. 30, 2026, across nine states, according to FinanceBuzz . The bank has also filed notices with the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) to close eight additional branches across seven states. These filings indicate planned closures rather than locations that have already shut down. Combined, the completed and planned shutdowns would affect 31 branches across 16 states. States where branches have already closed include: Arizona: 1 California: 6 Illinois: 1 Indiana: 2 New Jersey: 3 New York: 3 Texas: 5 Washington: 1 Wisconsin: 1 States with additional branches slated for closure include: Arizona: 2 Florida: 1 Indiana: 1 Kentucky: 1 Louisiana: 1 New York: 1 Ohio: 1 The latest shutdowns follow earlier reductions in the bank’s physical footprint throughout 2026. Chase submitted at least 16 notifications of branch closures from March through April 2026, according to OCC filings reported by TheStreet . The bank also shuttered eight branches across Florida, Washington, Ohio, Illinois, California, Louisiana, Arizona, and New York from June through July 2026. During the same period, Chase relocated four branches in Illinois, Ohio, and Florida, according to OCC filings reported by Fast Company . For consumers, these changes can mean traveling farther to access in-person banking services, particularly in communities where nearby branches are consolidated or eliminated. Customers who regularly deposit cash or need assistance with complicated transactions may be particularly affected. Chase closes dozens of retail branches, with more shutdowns to come. Tomas Abad / Getty Images Is Chase shrinking its retail branch network? Despite the closures, Chase is not necessarily shrinking its overall physical footprint. The bank continues to invest in its branch network, opening new locations and renovating existing ones as it adjusts its presence across different markets. In February 2026, Chase announced plans to open more than 160 new branches in over 30 states and renovate nearly 600 locations this year, according to a company announcement . Here’s some of my previous coverage of bank closures: Wells Fargo shuts down dozens of branches as more closures loom 169-year-old bank to close 26 branches in major shift 70-year-old bank chain closing 51 locations across 13 states The move is part of a multibillion-dollar investment toward its multiyear growth strategy, launched in 2024, to expand access to affordable and convenient financial services nationwide. The initiative aims to open more than 500 new branches, renovate 1,700 locations, and hire 3,500 employees in the U.S. over three years. “Our Community Centers are designed to make banking accessible and approachable for everyone,” Chase Head of Community and Business Development Diedra Porché said in the announcement. Chase recorded 5,164 branches as of Sept. 30, 2026, an increase of 3% from the prior year, according to the company’s third-quarter 2026 earnings report . The increase suggests that the latest closures are part of a broader effort to reposition the bank’s physical network rather than a retreat from traditional banking. By closing some locations while opening or renovating others, Chase can adjust its presence to population shifts, local demand, and changing customer preferences . Digital banking grows in popularity among consumers Consumer preferences have increasingly shifted toward digital financial services , changing how Americans interact with their banks. A Morning Consult survey conducted on behalf of the American Bankers Association (ABA) from Oct. 9 to Oct. 12, 2026, found that 44% of U.S. bank customers most often use mobile banking apps to manage their accounts. Another 20% use online banking through a laptop or desktop, while 10% most often visit a physical bank branch. The survey included 4,402 adults and had a margin of error of plus or minus one percentage point. “Americans greatly appreciate their banks’ online and mobile offerings and ability to choose from a wide variety of banking options that best meet their needs,” said ABA President and CEO Rob Nichols. However, the growing popularity of digital banking does not mean physical branches have become obsolete. In-person services remain important for customers who prefer speaking with bank employees, particularly when handling complicated transactions, depositing cash, or seeking financial guidance. “Branch closures increase the distance people must travel from where they live, shop, work or otherwise prefer to engage in financial transactions,” wrote Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis Industry Experts Drew Dahl, Michelle Franke, and James Fuchs. “Those affected sometimes have to go without or must drive long distances to access them.” As digital banking continues to reshape consumer habits, Chase’s expansion plans suggest physical branches remain an important part of its long-term strategy. Rather than eliminating traditional banking locations, the bank appears to be adjusting where and how it operates them to reflect changing customer needs . title: Costco sells something consumers want even if they don't need it
summary: Members keep buying things they don't need and feel good about it.
content: As we head into the holiday season, consumers have cut back on discretionary spending in order to pay for the cost of the season. “The majority (71%) of consumers are planning on cutting back to afford the holidays this year. Their own clothes, beauty, and personal purchases are the first to be cut (44%), followed by groceries and dining out (37%),” according to The Consumer Collective’s new “Give and Take: The State of Holiday Shopping in America 2026 .” Costco understands this and has leaned into delivering affordable indulgences that allow people to treat themselves without breaking their budget. That’s a strategy both Starbucks and McDonald’s have embraced, which has helped them continue to grow sales, even while Americans cut back their discretionary spending. For Costco, it’s a sales driver that adds to the perceived value of its membership. Consumers can do their regular shopping at the chain, fill up their cars with cheap gas, and get themselves a little something extra. Costco leans into affordable indulgence Costco’s food court has always leaned into the affordable indulgence model. Nobody feels bad treating themselves to a $1.50 hot dog, or even a $2.99 ice cream sundae. The warehouse club, however, has also leaned into offering strong value in its bakery department, giving members another way to treat themselves while they’re buying the items they actually need. “Growth in bakery reflects our success in adding new and indulgent items at great value for our members. An example of this is our in-house pastries, which grew by over 100% in the quarter,” CFO Gary Millerchip shared during the chain’s fourth-quarter earnings call . That, he noted, is part of a broader trend where members have shown a willingness to treat themselves, even as they face high gas prices and overall economic uncertainty. “Our members continue to show resilience in their spending, and they show a willingness to spend in discretionary areas where they’re seeing exciting new items at great value,” he added. Americans want treats Both Starbucks and McDonald’s have shown that even when budgets are tight, consumers want to do something nice for themselves. RTM Nexus CEO Dominick Miserandino told TheStreet that the idea of “affordable indulgence” allows people to treat themselves without feeling like they’ve made a bad financial decision. More Costco: Walmart takes aim at Costco with a new shopping perk Aldi cuts prices in a move that could pressure Costco Costco makes a seasonal food court change He noted that McDonald’s has been going after this audience with its new beverage line. “We have an issue of economy, and I think a McDonald’s is that low entry point, and if all you want to do is have a drink and feel special, that McDonald’s entry point might be the trick,” he wrote. Starbucks CFO Catherine Smith explained the customer behavior her chain has seen during its fourth-quarter earnings call . “In the U.S., consumers are increasingly prioritizing experiences that feel worth it. That reinforces our focus on quality, craft and connection and on delivering a consistently great customer experience,” she said. As a regular Starbucks customer, I can back that up. I get a drink from the chain nearly every day, and it’s an important ritual where I take a break from work and treat myself a little bit. Yes, it’s pricey for what it is, and I have a fancy espresso machine at home, but it’s important to do something for yourself, even if it’s just a small gesture. Costco’s food court also offers affordable indulgences. Shutterstock Bakery treats let Costco customers indulge While Starbucks costs more than many other coffee options, Costco actually offers bakery treats at value prices. Zappi CMO Nataly Kelly told Inc. that consumers are still treating themselves, despite higher costs. Instead of going to a specialty dessert shop, they are now choosing to buy treats at Costco. She also added that a fresh bakery is hard to replicate online or at a discount retailer, giving Costco an advantage. “Bakery gives Costco a high-margin, high-appeal reason to walk in on top of the staples,” she said. Costco sells baked goods at lower prices than Starbucks. It’s also cheaper than Kroger, Publix, and other grocery chains. That makes buying these not exactly necessary treats feel like a responsible way to do something nice for yourself, and perhaps your family. Yes, you’re buying something you don’t need, but the value justifies the expense. Related: Another healthy fast-food chain closes all its restaurants

title: CVS is open on Thanksgiving, but customers should check one important detail
summary: The pharmacy chain confirmed its Thanksgiving plans to TheStreet as new research reveals the cost of last-minute holiday shopping.
content: Thanksgiving Day can bring unexpected trips to the store, whether it’s to pick up a forgotten ingredient, grab extra snacks or purchase medicine. But finding a store that’s open on Thursday, Nov. 26, will be more challenging as many of the nation’s largest retailers continue to give employees Thanksgiving Day off. Walmart , Target and Costco are among the major retailers closing their stores for the holiday, as TheStreet previously reported. However, shoppers will still have some options, including at some of the nation’s largest pharmacy chains. CVS Health (CVS) confirmed its Thanksgiving Day plans to TheStreet on Wednesday, Nov. 25, though customers shouldn’t assume their neighborhood store or pharmacy will operate on its regular schedule. Also Read: Target closes all stores on Thanksgiving, but has a Black Friday surprise The holiday hours come as new research commissioned by CVS Pharmacy sheds light on how much those unexpected shopping trips can add to consumers’ holiday budgets. Last-minute holiday purchases add an average of $155 to shoppers’ budgets, according to the survey, which also found that some consumers make more than five panic trips to stores to finish their holiday shopping. With just four weeks between Thanksgiving and Christmas this year, shoppers have a limited window to finish their holiday purchases. And for those who need to fill a prescription or pick up over-the-counter medicine on Thanksgiving, checking pharmacy hours separately from store hours could be especially important. More Retail: Kohl’s confirms store closures during a critical shopping week Best Buy sticks with major nationwide store closure plans JCPenney’s Black Friday sale starts early, but an old tradition remains CVS confirms Thanksgiving Day store and pharmacy hours “CVS Pharmacy locations will be open on Thanksgiving Day, although some stores and/or pharmacies may have reduced hours,” Roslyn Guarino, senior manager of corporate communications at CVS Health, told TheStreet. “We recommend that customers call their local store before visiting or check hours at cvs.com .” Customers should confirm both retail store and pharmacy hours before heading out, particularly if they need to pick up a prescription. Walgreens is also opening stores on Thanksgiving , reversing its previous holiday policy. Some grocery chains, including Whole Foods Market , will also have locations open on Thanksgiving. Graphic: Kelly Tyko/TheStreet CVS survey reveals the cost of last-minute holiday shopping As consumers look for ways to stretch their holiday budgets, last-minute purchases could make that more difficult. CVS Pharmacy commissioned Talker Research to conduct an online survey of 2,000 Americans who celebrate a winter holiday. The survey was conducted from Sept. 22 to Sept. 28, 2026. While 51% of respondents said holiday shopping should be completed by mid-November, one in five admitted to being last-minute shoppers. Among the survey’s other findings: Last-minute purchases add an average of $155 to holiday budgets. One in 10 respondents make more than five panic trips to stores to finish holiday shopping. Seasonal snacks, stocking stuffers and finishing touches for holiday outfits are among the reasons for last-minute purchases. 30% plan to cut back on lavish gifts this year. 29% plan to be more careful about spending on holiday snacks. The survey findings highlight the challenge consumers face in balancing holiday traditions with affordability. Related: New penny law gives stores a surprising option for cash shoppers

title: Kroger is open on Thanksgiving, but there's a catch
summary: Shoppers can still make a last-minute grocery run on the holiday, but stores will close early as the company works to strengthen its business and keep prices competitive.
content: Thanksgiving dinner has a way of requiring just one more trip to the grocery store. Maybe it’s a bundle of herbs, a quart of whipping cream, or a bottle of wine you need to finish your menu. No matter how well I plan, there is always that one little thing that I somehow forgot, and I’m forced to make a last-minute Turkey-Day run. My favorite market is Trader Joe’s, but they’re not open on Thanksgiving. My second choice, Raley’s, is open on Thanksgiving, but only until 3 p.m. For shoppers who rely on Kroger, there is still an opportunity to make that last-minute run on Thanksgiving. Unlike several major retailers that close for the holiday, Kroger plans to keep its stores open on Thursday, Nov. 26, 2026. The holiday comes as Kroger works to sharpen its competitive position under CEO Greg Foran. The company reported modest sales growth in its latest quarter and is pursuing a new strategy focused on customer value, fresh food, digital sales, and more efficient operations. Also read: Publix confirms a storewide decision holiday shoppers will notice What are Kroger’s Thanksgiving 2026 hours? Shoppers will need to plan ahead: Kroger stores will be open on Thanksgiving Day, but they will close at 5 p.m., according to the company’s official holiday-hours page . The company’s pharmacies and clinics will be closed on Thanksgiving. Kroger says normal hours will resume Friday, Nov. 27. Related: Grocery stores open on Thanksgiving include Whole Foods, but hours are limited Customers should check their individual store’s schedule before making a trip, particularly if they shop at a Kroger-operated grocery banner. Store hours and pharmacy services can vary by location. Kroger operates grocery stores under a number of familiar names, including: Baker’s City Market Dillons Food 4 Less Foods Co. Fred Meyer Fry’s Gerbes Harris Teeter King Soopers Mariano’s Metro Market Pay-Less Super Markets Pick ‘n Save QFC Ralphs Smith’s Food and Drug Customers can use the Kroger store locator to check local information about holiday hours. Kroger locations will be open until 5 p.m. on Thanksgiving Day 2026. cbarnesphotography / Getty Images Kroger’s latest financial results show a mixed picture Kroger’s latest reported financial results show that the grocery business is growing, although sales momentum remains a priority for management. In September, the company reported second-quarter 2026 results for the period ended Aug. 15. Identical sales, excluding fuel, increased just 0.2% from the year-earlier quarter. The company reported improvements in other areas, including digital sales and earnings. By the numbers: Kroger’s second-quarter 2026 results 0.2%: Increase in identical sales excluding fuel, according to Kroger’s Q2 earnings report 20%: Growth in adjusted eCommerce sales, according to the same earnings release $971 million: Operating profit, compared with $863 million in the prior-year quarter, according to Kroger’s earnings release $1.05: Earnings per share, compared with 91 cents a year earlier, according to Kroger’s Q2 report $1.09: Adjusted earnings per share, compared with $1.04 a year earlier, according to Kroger’s Q2 report Kroger also lowered its full-year 2026 forecast for identical sales excluding fuel. The company now expects growth of 0.2% to 0.8%, down from its earlier forecast of 1% to 2%. It maintained its full-year adjusted earnings-per-share forecast of $5.10 to $5.30. These figures are the company’s second-quarter results and full-year guidance, not completed fiscal-year results; Kroger is scheduled to release its next earnings report on Thursday, Dec. 3, 2026 , before the market opens, according to Zacks . New strategy puts customer value at the center Kroger is also trying to make its business more competitive with a strategy outlined at its Oct. 20, 2026, investor update. CEO Greg Foran said the company is focused on making value more visible to customers and directing resources toward areas where it sees the greatest returns. The plan has three main priorities: Win with the customer: Invest in fresh food, prepared meals, private-label products, and its Boost membership program. Grow digital sales profitably: Expand eCommerce and retail media, including Kroger Precision Marketing. Modernize operations: Find savings through more direct sourcing, streamlined processes, disciplined purchasing, and technology. Kroger also laid out longer-term financial targets at the October investor update. The company is aiming for approximately 3% comparable sales growth in 2029, excluding fuel and pharmacy, along with annual adjusted earnings-per-share growth of 7% to 11% from fiscal 2027 through fiscal 2029. Those are future targets, not current financial results. The company says cost savings and operational improvements will help fund investments in customer value and growth. Thanksgiving dinner is costing shoppers more Kroger’s focus on value comes as shoppers face higher costs for some traditional Thanksgiving foods. The American Farm Bureau Federation’s 2026 Thanksgiving dinner survey found that the average cost of a meal for 10 people reached $58.63, up 6% from 2025. That works out to about $5.86 per person. More Grocery: Costco makes a seasonal food court change More Kroger and Albertsons locations will close in 2026 Walmart copies a core Costco move that also benefits customers The increase was driven in part by higher prices for turkey, milk, dinner rolls, and cranberries. A 16-pound frozen turkey averaged $23.68, up 10% from the previous year. The figures do not measure Kroger’s prices specifically, but they help explain why grocery value remains a central issue for retailers heading into the holiday season. Kroger shoppers should get there early Kroger is giving Thanksgiving shoppers an option that many retailers do not: the ability to make a grocery run on the holiday itself. But the 5 p.m. closing time leaves a shorter window for anyone who forgets an ingredient or needs one more item for dinner. Pharmacies and clinics will be closed, and normal store hours are scheduled to resume Friday. For shoppers counting on Kroger for a last-minute Thanksgiving stop, checking local hours and getting there early may make the difference. title: Major discount chain collapses in insolvency, more than 11,000 jobs at risk
summary: The chain Poundland was founded in 1990 and currently has more than 600 stores.
content: The British High Street, which is the local term for a city’s main commercial thoroughfare and more metaphorically the nationwide brands that typically appear in central shopping areas, have faced a tough few years. Fashion brands such as Claire’s, River Island, and Russell and Bromley are among the chains that collectively closed hundreds of stores across the United Kingdom in 2026 amid a sharp drop-off in sales. Squeezed consumer budgets and a retail environment that has increasingly moved online have both contributed to this period of sustained decline, even for discount brands that had formerly been more resilient than the rest of the industry, Who What Wear noted. British discount variety chain Poundland collapses into administration This week, value variety chain and fashion retailer Poundland made headlines after entering administration. This is the British term for the insolvency process that is the closest equivalent to a Chapter 11 bankruptcy in the U.S. It requires a company unable to meet its financial obligations to hand over control to a court-appointed administrator , who will typically explore restructuring options to avoid liquidation. Founded by Dave Dodd and Steven Smith out of the West Midlands city of Walsall in 1990, Poundland expanded quickly to a national chain with more than 600 stores across the United Kingdom. Related: Domino’s Pizza franchisee files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy As an early player in stores selling low-cost versions of various popular grocery, toiletries, home, and household cleaning products, Poundland reached a mass audience quickly and went through different periods of loss and profit over the years. Poundland went from reporting a loss of £68 million to a profit of £18.1 million between 2025 and 2026 as more value-driven consumers increasingly sought affordable options of popular brands. Yet a central sticking point for the brand’s inability to find a new buyer is a £22.5 million shareholder loan that current owner Gordon Brothers inherited when it purchased Poundland from Pepco for a symbolic £1 in June 2025, as the BBC reported. Poundland Managing Director Barry Williams sent staff a note saying that the company had “no alternative but to take this decision” to enter administration after talks with several potential bidders around a discount deal ultimately fell through at the eleventh hour, and Gordon Brothers took away “all borrowing facilities and access to [Poundland’s] bank accounts” at the end of October. Poundland was acquired by U.S. hedge fund firm Gordon Brothers in 2025. ASphotowed / Getty Images An increasingly uncertain future for the Poundland chain “Under these circumstances, it is impossible for the board of directors to see how Poundland can continue to operate as a going concern,” Williams’ note reads further. While no disruptions to Poundland’s stores and distribution centers are being reported as the London-based corporate advisory firm AlixPartners embarks on the administration process, its future looks increasingly uncertain , given repeated failed efforts to find someone to take it over. More Retail And Travel News: Airline to launch unusual new flight to Cayman Islands from the U.S. Taco Bell to bring back five favorites after 20 years 153-year-old footwear retailer quietly closes 40 stores Low-cost airline launches easier way to get to Sri Lanka AlixPartners put out a call to “anybody interested in acquiring the business in part or as a whole” but also said it is pursuing all options to recoup losses. Should a buyer not be found, this could include the closure and liquidation of the physical stores and the sale of the brand. Poundland employs between 10,500 and 11,000 workers across the United Kingdom and Ireland. These jobs are also at risk, as even a best-case scenario will bring significant reductions. title: Some Amazon “best deals” might cost more during the sale
summary: Amazon fires back at a recent research revealing a key difference in defining “deals” that consumers should know.
content: As millions of consumers prepare their online carts ahead of Black Friday, planning to use holiday discounts to stretch their tight budgets, a recent study suggests shoppers be meticulous when picking gifts on Amazon. An estimated 182.7 million Americans plan to shop between Thanksgiving and Cyber Monday this year, according to the National Retail Federation . Roughly 82% say they are actively taking steps to keep holiday costs down. To actually save, consumers need to do more than just click on an item marked as a deal. A recent investigation suggests that many of the marquee discounts on the e-commerce retail giant may not save buyers a penny. Some items might even cost more during the sale than they did weeks earlier. There is a key detail in how Amazon defines a “deal” that every shopper should understand before checking out. Nearly 1 in 3 Black Friday Amazon “deals” offered no savings to shoppers, study claims Researchers at the economic policy group Groundwork Collaborative analyzed 351 unique products promoted on Amazon’s official deal pages, some marketed for Black Friday and others for Cyber Monday across 2024 and 2025, with only three items featured in both events. Groundwork Collaborative is an economic policy and advocacy organization led by President and CEO Lindsay Owens, a former economic policy adviser to Senator Elizabeth Warren. Its work focuses on consumer protection and corporate accountability, and it receives philanthropic funding, including support from the Fidelity Investments Charitable Gift Fund and the Thomas Thompson Trust. Using historical pricing records from the tracking service Keepa , the group compared each item’s sale price against its lowest price in the weeks leading up to the event. Some Amazon “best deals” might cost more during the sale, investigation finds. ullstein bild Dtl. / Getty Images The report’s key findings included: 29.1% of advertised deals cost the exact same or more during the sale than their lowest price in the previous 30 days. 9.4% of the deals, nearly 1 in 10, were priced higher during Black Friday or Cyber Monday than in the month before. When researchers looked back 90 days instead of 30, 57.3% of the products offered zero savings over their recent low, and 27% were more expensive. Half of the items that failed to beat their 30-day low had been sold at or below their “deal” price on at least eight separate days during the month prior, according to the Groundwork Collaborative report. “Shoppers trust that the deals advertised to them deliver real savings because Amazon promotes them that way,” Groundwork CEO Lindsay Owens stated when releasing the findings. Popular gift categories were hit hardest Shoppers buying gifts for kids, athletes, or tech fans faced the highest odds of encountering stagnant or inflated prices. In Sports & Outdoors, half of the studied deals offered no savings over their 30-day low. Toys & Games followed at 42.8%, while Electronics hit 38.6%. By contrast, only 13.5% of Beauty deals failed to beat their recent low. The report highlighted several well-known brands among the examples: A 46mm Apple Watch Series 10 carried a $679.99 price tag during Black Friday 2025, which was 13% higher than its price nearly a month earlier. A Carhartt knit beanie advertised at $19.77 for Cyber Monday 2025 had sold for $14.74 just 10 days before the event, a 34% markup over its recent low. Beats Solo 4 headphones listed at $129.95 on Black Friday 2025 had already been available at that exact price 12 days earlier. A Fitbit Charge 6 marked at $99.95 for Cyber Monday 2025 matched its price from 20 days prior. Amazon fires back, and exposes a key rule In an official statement on About Amazon , the retail giant said the report relied on a “cherry-picked, unrepresentative sample” of roughly 350 items out of more than 10 million deals offered across its 2024 and 2025 holiday events. Amazon noted that the study included only 17 of its top 200 best-selling deals. It also said Groundwork mistakenly counted some items with strikethrough reference prices that never carried an official deal badge and treated early-access event discounts as pre-sale prices. Under Amazon’s internal rules, a product must be priced “at or below its lowest price over the prior 30 days” to earn a deal badge. “When we looked at the research’s actual deals for 2025, we found that 89% of the products had lower prices and 10% were the same, compared with the prior 30-day low price,” Amazon stated . That wording reveals the catch for shoppers. Because Amazon’s rule allows a deal badge when an item matche s its 30-day low, a product that dropped in price two weeks before Black Friday can carry a bright holiday deal banner without dropping a single cent further on the big day. “The biggest gap between the two sides is timing,” according to Techlicious . TheStreet’s check of Keepa’s price history for the Fitbit Charge 6 shows how that timing works in practice. The tracker was listed at $99.95 on Nov. 2, 2025, rose back to $159.95 on Nov. 10, then gradually declined and returned to $99.95 on Nov. 20, where it stayed through Jan. 14, 2026. Because the Nov. 2 price falls within 30 days of Cyber Monday (Dec. 1), the $99.95 tag matched rather than beat the 30-day low. That is enough to qualify as a deal under Amazon’s rule, even though shoppers could have paid the same price in early November. Related: Shoppers ditch Hostess snack cakes while Uncrustables sell faster than factories can make them How to protect your wallet before checking out Online holiday spending is projected to hit $12.9 billion on Black Friday alone and $15.1 billion on Cyber Monday, according to Adobe’s 2026 holiday forecast . Consumers are already leaning on technology to fight back. Nearly three in five Thanksgiving weekend shoppers (59%) plan to use AI tools this year to compare prices, track budgets, and scan retailer sites, the National Retail Federation found. Before clicking “buy” on Amazon this weekend, four quick checks can confirm whether a discount is real: Ask Alexa for the price chart : Amazon’s built-in Alexa shopping assistant can display up to 365 days of an item’s price history right on the product page, according to Amazon . Use free third-party trackers: Browser tools like CamelCamelCamel and Keepa show lifetime price graphs for Amazon listings. If it’s at a one-year low and already on your list, buy it. If it was cheaper weeks ago, set a price alert and wait, advises Techlicious . Compare across big-box rivals : Major competitors like Walmart and Target run overlapping holiday sales and price-match policies that can undercut a stagnant Amazon listing. Avoid scrolling: Elizabeth Pancotti, vice president of policy, advocacy and research at Groundwork Collaborative, advises skipping endless big-box deal feeds in favor of smaller retailers offering flat store-wide discounts, though due diligence still applies, reported BBC . title: Target shares key update on the fun side of its business
summary: The retail giant is seeing huge success in a category consumers love.
content: There was a time when a quick trip to Target just wasn’t a thing. You went in for paper towels or groceries and somehow left with a new throw pillow, a seasonal decoration, a board game, or some other item you didn’t need after spending 90 minutes roaming the aisles. That was part of Target’s appeal. Shopping at Target once felt less like running errands and more like discovering new fun merchandise at every turn. But over the years, as Target faced mounting competition and struggled with merchandise that didn’t always excite shoppers, some of that magic appeared to fade. Now, Target is trying to bring it back, and one of the more surprising parts of its business is showing that the strategy may be working. Target’s fun business is growing Target’s Fun 101 merchandise category is experiencing impressive growth, with sales increasing at an impressive rate, according to the company’s third-quarter earnings call . Even more interesting is that the growth isn’t entirely dependent on one particularly hot product category. During the earnings call, Target CFO Jim Lee highlighted the strength of Fun 101, which includes toys, collectibles, sporting goods, gadgets and other entertainment-focused merchandise. “Year-to-date sales in Fun 101 have grown in the high teens, of which about 40% of this growth is from trading cards. However, even when excluding the benefit from trading cards, Fun 101 is still delivering double-digit growth,” Lee said . That distinction is important. Trading cards have become a major retail phenomenon, with collectors and fans hunting for popular releases, including Pokémon cards and sports collectibles. Target has benefited from that enthusiasm. But the company’s results suggest shoppers are also spending more across the broader category. During the third quarter, Fun 101 sales jumped nearly 27% compared with the previous year, making it one of Target’s strongest-performing merchandise categories. The results indicate that consumers are responding to more than collectibles. They’re finding reasons to browse the toy aisles, discover new products, and spend money on items that make shopping feel entertaining again. Target’s Fun 101 category includes toys, collectibles, sporting goods, gadgets, and other entertainment-focused merchandise. Bloomberg / Getty Images Target wants to become a destination for pop culture Target isn’t simply relying on popular trading cards to drive sales. The company is deliberately reshaping its merchandise strategy to make Fun 101 a destination for all types of customers. Target’s management has emphasized the importance of identifying consumer trends early and making strategic investments in products that shoppers are excited about. That includes building out its assortment of toys, sports-related merchandise, collectibles, and gadgets. Target has also expanded its sports fan shops across more than 1,600 stores. Target is trying to bring back its shopping magic Fun 101 isn’t the only category delivering growth. Target reported 9% growth in beauty and nearly 7% growth in food and beverage during the third quarter. Overall, comparable sales increased 5.6%, supported by a 5% increase in customer traffic. These numbers suggest that shoppers are beginning to respond to the retailer’s broader efforts to improve its merchandise assortment and shopping experience. Of course, Target still has work to do, particularly in apparel and home, where management has acknowledged that its offerings need improvement. But the strength of Fun 101 provides an encouraging example of what can happen when Target gives shoppers products they genuinely want to discover. Maurie Backman owns shares of Target. title: Will Trader Joe's be open on Thanksgiving Day 2026?
summary: The specialty retailer does not close its doors as often as some other grocers.
content: Thanksgiving grocery shopping can be stressful even when everything goes according to plan. Shoppers are juggling crowded stores, rising food costs, and the pressure to get everything on the table before guests arrive. I love Thanksgiving — the meal planning, table-setting, and of course, having my kids home. But no matter how organized I am, and how many lists I make, I almost always find myself in need of an egg, a cup of heavy cream, or one more stick of butter on Thanksgiving Day. Not this year, though. I made my lists, checked them three times, and went to Costco over the weekend and Trader Joe’s on the morning of Nov. 24. I’m hoping this will be the first year I don’t have to run out to pick up any last-minute ingredients on Wednesday night or, even worse, on Thanksgiving Day. I learned the hard way a couple of years ago that my go-to grocery store, Trader Joe’s, is not open on Thanksgiving Day. Trader Joe’s is among the retailers that close their doors for the holiday. Unlike some grocery chains that operate on reduced holiday schedules, such as my other go-to, Raley’s, the company shuts down all its stores nationwide. The policy is particularly important for budget-minded shoppers who rely on the specialty grocer for a turkey, potatoes, fresh herbs, and seasonal products. And with grocery bills still a concern for American households, getting shopping done ahead of time can make a difference. Also read: Publix confirms a storewide decision holiday shoppers will notice Grocery prices remain a concern for holiday shoppers Food inflation has made grocery shopping more expensive over the past several years, even though the pace of price increases has slowed. According to the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Food Price Outlook , grocery prices increased in 2026, and the agency’s November 2026 report projected that food-at-home prices would rise 1% in 2027. Restaurant and food-service prices were forecast to increase 2.8%. More Grocery: Costco makes a seasonal food court change More Kroger and Albertsons locations will close in 2026 Walmart copies a core Costco move that also benefits customers The Bureau of Labor Statistics’ October 2026 Consumer Price Index showed that grocery prices increased 0.4% from September to October. Food-away-from-home prices rose 0.5% during the same period. The BLS noted that October 2025 data were unavailable because of the government shutdown, so a normal year-over-year comparison could not be calculated. For shoppers preparing Thanksgiving dinner, those increases can add up, particularly when buying meat, vegetables, dairy products, alcohol, and other holiday staples. Families hosting the holiday this year plan to spend an average of $427 on food, drinks, and supplies, according to a LendingTree survey . That’s up from $414 a year earlier. It’s no wonder that about a third of potential hosts say hosting is a financial strain, the LendingTree survey also found. Among those planning to celebrate Thanksgiving, 53% say inflation is affecting their plans or budget, with 25% changing food choices, 22% using more coupons, and 14% reducing the guest list. The American Farm Bureau Federation’s annual Thanksgiving dinner survey offers another way to measure the impact on consumers. Its 2026 survey found that a traditional Thanksgiving meal for 10 people cost an average of $58.63, or about $5.86 per person. That was a 6% increase from 2025. The survey also found that a 16-pound frozen turkey averaged $23.68, up 10% from the previous year. The 2027 survey will be worth watching as another measure of what holiday shoppers are paying for the traditional meal. Families hosting Thanksgiving this year plan to spend an average of $427 on food, drinks, and supplies. Drazen Zigic / Getty Images Trader Joe’s will close all stores on Thanksgiving Trader Joe’s closes its stores nationwide on three holidays each year: New Year’s Day, Thanksgiving Day, and Christmas Day. The retailer has discussed the policy in its Inside Trader Joe’s podcast , explaining that the three closures give employees an opportunity to spend time with family and friends. Thanksgiving falls on Thursday, Nov. 26, in 2027. That means shoppers who need last-minute ingredients, appetizers, desserts, or other holiday essentials will need to make their purchases before stores close Wednesday evening. The company also operates on a reduced schedule for certain other holidays. Shoppers can check individual store information through Trader Joe’s store locator . Other retailers also close on Thanksgiving Trader Joe’s is not alone in giving employees Thanksgiving Day off. Several major retailers have adopted similar policies, although holiday schedules can vary by company and year. Among the retailers that have traditionally closed on Thanksgiving are: Target confirmed in a holiday announcement that all stores would close on Thanksgiving Day. Walmart also confirmed in its 2026 holiday schedule that it will be closed on Thursday. Sam’s Club: Check the company’s official holiday and club information . Even though I’ve sworn up and down that I will not have any last-minute food needs on Thursday, I can also sleep easy knowing that the Raley’s up the street will be open until 3 p.m. on Thanksgiving Day. When will Trader Joe’s reopen? Trader Joe’s stores have traditionally resumed regular operations on Friday following Thanksgiving. Most locations generally operate from 8 a.m. to 9 p.m., although hours can vary by store. Customers can use the company’s store locator to confirm local operating hours before making the trip. title: When Walmart, Target, Costco, and other major retailers open on Black Friday
summary: Store opening times, deals worth watching, and advice to help you avoid Black Friday shopping mistakes
content: Black Friday no longer starts on Thanksgiving, like it did during my childhood. People used to literally finish their holiday dinner, then head to the mall. At some point, people realized that opening on the actual holiday was cruel to employees, and nearly every major chain pushed the unofficial start of the year’s biggest shopping season back to the Friday after Thanksgiving. Many retailers, however, will open their doors early and offer special deals to entice shoppers to come to them first. Once you get them in the store, it’s a much easier conversion event. Plus, it speaks straight to people’s wallets,” he told TheStreet. TheStreet Black Friday 2026: Store hours and key offerings at 9 big retailers Here’s a look at when the nine biggest retail chains in the United States will open on Black Friday and what their biggest promotions will be. Some stores may follow different hours, so please check with your local retailer before heading out. Walmart Hours: Black Friday begins at 12:01 a.m. EST on Walmart.com and in stores at 6 a.m. local time. Offerings: Thousands of gifts under $20 and 25 toys on this year’s list priced under $25. Walmart+: Select online-only deals reserved exclusively for Walmart+ members for the first 24 hours, while supplies last. Source: Walmart Amazon Hours: Big Deals drop twice on Black Friday, at midnight and 8 a.m. PST. Offerings: Up to 35% off Amazon devices; up to $600 off select Sony and Hisense TVs. Also: Up to $500 off select Balsam Hill and Fraser Hill Farm artificial Christmas trees. Source: Amazon Costco Hours: Costco does not universally have special Black Friday hours, but some clubs will open early. Offerings: Deals are while supplies last, featuring holiday decor, Bissell, Dyson, and Shark vacuums, and Keurig and Nespresso machines. Source: Costco Home Depot Hours: Open at 6 a.m. Offerings: Select power tool BOGOs. Buy a participating RYOBI, Milwaukee, or DEWALT tool or battery kit, get a free select power tool. Source: Home Depot Walgreens Hours: Walgreens stores and pharmacies will operate under their regular posted hours on Black Friday. All Walgreens stores will actually be open on Thanksgiving , with most open 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. and about 4,000 pharmacies open. Offerings: No Black Friday-specific deals listed. Source: Walgreens Target Hours: Stores open at 6 a.m. and close at the current closing time. Giveaway: The first 100 eligible guests at every store on Nov. 27 get a $25, $50, or $100 gift card. One guest per store gets a $1,000 gift card. Offerings: Up to 50% off select toys, 40% off beauty gift sets, and 40% off holiday trees. Exclusives: POP MART gifts, a special BTS book, and Topps NBA trading cards. Source: Target Best Buy Hours: Open 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. on Black Friday Doorbuster: My Best Buy members can buy a $100 Best Buy Gift Card for $60, in-store only on Nov. 27; at least 50 cards per store, limit one per person. Offerings: MacBook Air 13-inch for $1,049 ($250 off); TCL 65-inch TV for $229.99 ($240 off). Also, Sony WH-1000XM5 headphones for $169 ($229 off); Shark PowerDetect cordless stick vacuum for $199.99 ($300 off). Source : Best Buy Kohl’s Hours: Open at 5 a.m. on Black Friday. Giveaway: First 200 shoppers at every store get $5 to $100 in instant Kohl’s Cash, while supplies last, redeemable in store that day only Offerings: Doorbusters on Kohls.com from 12:01 a.m. CST on Thanksgiving and in stores Nov. 27 to 28. Source: Kohl’s Dick’s Sporting Goods Hours: Doors open on Black Friday at 6 a.m. Offerings: Up to 30% off select Nike clothing and shoes; deals run Nov. 22 to Dec. 5. Source: Dick’s Sporting Goods Black Friday no longer starts on Thanksgiving, but many retailers will open their doors early and offer special deals. Shutterstock Tips from a former retailer on Black Friday Back in my days running a large independent toy store, we actually didn’t do huge business on Black Friday. Our holiday season started to pick up over the weekend, and it was madness pretty much until a few days after New Year’s. We brought in a lot of merchandise specifically for the holiday and offered the best prices we could. That’s not always what the big chains do, so I recommend following some simple rules around larger purchases. Know the pre-sale price: Just because an item says 50% off doesn’t mean it wasn’t cheaper a week ago. For all big-ticket purchases, do your homework and know the pre-holiday price. Compare apples to apples: Big retailers might sell similar versions of a product with fewer features at a lower price. That happens a lot with TVs and computers. You might still get a deal as the dropped features may not be things you miss, but know what you’re getting. Don’t buy into scarcity: Overpaying for the hottest thing is a mistake. It might make the holidays less festive, but sometimes waiting until January to buy, after demand has dropped, gets you better prices. Buy for the person getting the gift: We sold a lot of rock tumblers and slot car sets at the toy store that maybe Dad wanted more than their child. Focus on the happiness of the person getting the gift, not what you wish they liked. Related: Costco sells something consumers want even if they don’t need it

title: Don't let a market selloff wreck your retirement plan
summary: Market selloffs are more common than we might think; investors need a plan to ensure they don't derail their retirement
content: Last week we saw a steep market selloff that pushed all three major market indexes into correction territory. While this doesn’t happen every day, steep corrections are also not that uncommon. Investors need to be prepared for these market drops, especially investors in or near retirement. Vanguard says that market volatility is an expected, if uncomfortable, part of investing. A sharp market drop can test even seasoned investors—especially when headlines scream about tech pullbacks, shifting rate expectations, or slipping account balances. For workers building a nest egg and retirees drawing income, a selloff’s biggest threat isn’t temporary volatility on paper; it’s making permanent mistakes at the wrong time. You don’t need to predict the next market bottom to protect your retirement plan. Instead, focus on structural guardrails that keep short-term swings from derailing long-term goals. Separate near-term cash from long-term growth If you are retired or within a few years of leaving work, forced stock sales during a downturn can lock in losses and accelerate portfolio depletion—a challenge known as sequence-of-returns risk . Keeping one to two years of living expenses in cash, money market funds, or short-duration Treasuries gives you a buffer so you aren’t selling depressed equities just to pay bills. Rebalance instead of reacting Market swings naturally pull your asset allocation off target. Rebalancing—trimming areas that held up better and adding back to beaten-down segments according to a set rule—enforces “buy low, sell high” discipline without relying on gut instinct. Elevated bond yields in recent years have also given fixed income a more meaningful role in stabilizing multi-asset portfolios. It’s important for retirees and those approaching retirement to have a solid long-term portfolio plan that addresses periodic market downturns. Keep contributions going—or pace withdrawals smartly Still accumulating? Continuing regular 401(k) or IRA contributions during a dip lets you buy shares at lower prices, even if quarterly statements look bumpy. Already taking income? Consider temporarily trimming discretionary withdrawals, delaying non-essential big-ticket purchases, or leaning on guaranteed income sources such as Social Security or pensions to ease pressure on your portfolio. Use market dips for tax and Roth moves Tax-loss harvesting (taxable accounts): Selling losing positions can offset realized capital gains—plus up to $3,000 of ordinary income per year—while reinvesting in a similar (but not substantially identical) fund keeps you in position for a rebound. Opportunistic Roth conversions (pre-tax IRAs): Converting depressed traditional retirement balances can lower the tax hit on the converted amount, allowing a future recovery to compound tax-free. How retirement savers can respond to a selloff Strategy Best Fit Key Benefit Watch-Out Cash / Short-Term Buffer Near-retirees & retirees Prevents forced selling in down markets Cash drag if held far beyond near-term needs Systematic Rebalancing All long-term investors Restores target risk and captures mean reversion Can trigger taxes if done in taxable accounts Flexible Spending Guardrails Retirees drawing portfolio income Extends portfolio longevity during drawdowns Requires willingness to curb discretionary outlays Tax-Loss / Roth Moves Savers with taxable or IRA assets Turns paper dips into long-term tax efficiency Watch wash-sale rules and tax-bracket thresholds More Retirement: Annuities can be a retirement safety net to prevent outliving savings How retirees over 70 ½ can cut RMD taxes with a QCD Self-directed IRA pitfalls: one mistake can blow up your retirement The bottom line: a market selloff is uncomfortable, but your retirement plan should be built for full cycles—not calm stretches alone. Anchoring on liquidity, disciplined rebalancing, and tax-smart adjustments helps protect your savings without abandoning your long-term strategy. title: Fidelity's latest data has a strong warning for retirement savers
summary: Fidelity just flagged what could quietly chip away at a seven-figure retirement account.
content: A small dip in a savings rate rarely makes the evening news. Still, Fidelity’s third-quarter report shows the slowdown wasn’t limited to 401(k) plans, with 403(b) savers also trimming their total rate to 11.8%, according to Fidelity Investments . The bright spot is that 96.4% of workers kept or raised their contributions during the quarter. Then there’s the question of how much is enough. Affluent Americans with at least $100,000 in investable assets now say they’d need roughly $2.6 million before they can retire comfortably, Fortune reported . So even a $2 million balance isn’t a finish line. The same habits that got you there still have to carry you the rest of the way. Saving less is a habit that compounds Fidelity’s numbers show where the gap sits. Workers contributed 9.6% of pay on average while employers added 4.7%, which leaves the typical saver just short of the firm’s 15% target. Boomers and Gen X are the exceptions, and both still clear that bar comfortably, according to Fidelity Investments . Washington is making it a little easier to catch up. The IRS raised the 2027 401(k) limit to $25,500 from $24,500 and lifted the catch-up for savers 50 and older to $8,500. That gives older workers in most plans room to put away up to $34,000 next year. Also read: Ford and BMW are watching China for a troubling new reason There’s a catch for high earners, though. Workers who made more than $155,000 from their employer generally must make catch-up contributions on a Roth basis, and the test looks back at 2026 pay. “That last threshold is based on 2026 wages, NOT 2027 wages!” said Jeff Levine of Focus Partners. Lower expected returns make every saved dollar more important. Fidelity projects U.S. stocks will return about 5.8% a year over the next 20 years, while Vanguard’s 10-year range runs from 4.8% to 6.8%, roughly half the 10% many retirement calculators assume. If markets really do slow down, savers can’t count on growth alone to make up for smaller contributions. Every withdrawal costs more than it looks Pulling money out early has become surprisingly common. Earlier this year, Vanguard reported that 6% of its 401(k) participants took hardship withdrawals in 2025, up from 5% a year before, CBS News reported . Avoiding foreclosure or eviction and covering medical bills topped the list of reasons people gave. And the penalty is only part of the bill. Pull money from a traditional or Roth IRA before age 59½ without a qualifying reason, and you’ll generally owe a 10% penalty plus regular income tax. What hurts more over time is that the money stops growing. Twenty years of lost compounding can cost far more than the penalty ever did. Wealthy retirees face a different version of the same trap: selling at the wrong moment. Charles Schwab suggests keeping roughly a year of spending in cash, after guaranteed income, plus two to four years in short-term bonds. That kind of cushion lets retirees leave their stocks alone when markets slump. Plenty of people still haven’t planned for the long haul. More than half of Americans say it’s at least somewhat likely they’ll outlive their savings, and 35% admit they haven’t taken any steps to deal with that risk, according to 24/7 Wall St . Even a large balance can run thin when retirement stretches for 30 years or more. Wealthy retirees face a different version of the same trap, which is selling at the wrong moment. FinkAvenue / Getty Images The 4% rule needs a reality check The old 4% rule says $2 million gives you $80,000 to spend in year one. Morningstar now puts the safer starting rate at 3.9% for 2026. That’s a meaningful step down from the old rule. Some planners have dropped the fixed-rate idea altogether, preferring to adjust spending year by year, depending on what markets do. How the portfolio is built matters just as much. About a quarter of retirees hold more than 80% of their balance in stocks. Those with at least $1 million saved are three times as likely to run that kind of aggressive mix. More Retirement Savings: Vanguard flags a retirement fear built into 401(k) plans Americans’ retirement savings face a hidden drain Charles Schwab flags vital 401(k) maxing reality Going heavy on equities right at the start of retirement can backfire badly if markets turn when withdrawals are already underway. Rising health costs chip away at income, too. Social Security’s 3.6% cost-of-living increase lifts the average retired worker’s monthly check to $2,170. But the standard Medicare Part B premium climbs to $209.40 in 2027. For many retirees, part of that raise is gone before it ever hits their bank account. Higher-income retirees pay even more. Medicare surcharges kick in for individuals with modified adjusted gross income above $112,000. And about 9% of Part B enrollees pay them. A large IRA withdrawal in a single year can push a $2 million household over that line without much warning. Taxes can quietly drain a seven-figure account RMDs trip up a lot of wealthy retirees. At 73, the IRS starts requiring withdrawals from traditional 401(k)s and IRAs, and every dollar pulled out gets taxed as ordinary income. A big enough withdrawal can quietly push someone into a higher tax bracket. Roth IRAs aren’t subject to that rule, which is why converting gradually, while there’s still time, is something a lot of planners bring up well before a client turns 73. Forget one, and it gets costly fast. A missed RMD comes with a 25% excise tax, though that drops to 10% if you fix it within two years. Still, only 14% of retirees have a detailed plan for their RMDs. Sketching out withdrawals a few years in advance is one of the easiest ways to keep the tax bill in check. In the end, the best defense is still plain discipline. “What stands out this quarter is the consistency we’re seeing from retirement savers,” said Sharon Brovelli , president of Workplace Investing. For a $2 million nest egg, steady habits in saving, spending, and withdrawing will likely matter more than any single swing in the market.
